slides.title: Hannah's Bread Company — Dynatrace migration
slides.subtitle: Cross-channel observability and mission-critical app monitoring · Leadership brief · 2026-05-28

slides._comment: Executive summary — lead with business impact, not telemetry
slides.title: Hannah's team learns of outages from staff and customers — not from monitoring
content: Hannah's is transitioning to Dynatrace® from Datadog across 30 U.S. and Canada facilities — a greenfield implementation with an urgency to move fast
Two mission-critical logistics apps (breadSHIP and breadSAIL) have significant performance issues and no Application Performance Monitoring (APM) visibility today

A fast-growing mobile ordering app — Hannah's newest direct revenue channel — has no performance instrumentation: failed orders, slow checkouts, and geographic gaps are invisible until a customer calls
National expansion is planned with no monitoring readiness indicators and no formal Service Level Objective (SLO) tracking in place

slides.title: All five gaps are confirmed — the monitoring safety net does not yet exist

cards.header: Outages discovered by staff, not IT
cards.body: No proactive Synthetic monitoring covers breadSHIP, breadSAIL, or the mobile app API
cards.subcopy: Datadog synthetic coverage scope is pending confirmation

cards.body: Baseline host inventory has not been completed — the full infrastructure gap is unknown
cards.subcopy: Dynatrace has zero coverage today; Datadog scope is pending the inventory

cards.body: No SLO tracking exists in Dynatrace; target values have not been formally agreed
cards.subcopy: SLO configuration requires a target-setting workshop as a prerequisite

cards.body: The mobile ordering app has no Real User Monitoring (RUM) across devices, browsers, or geographies
cards.subcopy: Hannah's fastest-growing revenue channel has no early warning signal

slides.title: Leadership learns of operational impact from logistics reports, not dashboards
content: No instrumented connection exists between application performance and business outcomes such as order delays, dispatch failures, or mobile conversion rates
When breadSHIP or breadSAIL fails, dock workers and yard coordinators cannot complete dispatch operations — risking spoilage and missed delivery windows — but IT only hears about it after the fact
The mobile ordering app has no conversion funnel instrumentation — whether a latency spike is costing orders is unknowable without business event tracking
Closing this gap is the highest-effort action in the plan, requiring application-layer instrumentation and logistics team coordination

slides.title: The plan — four serialized implementation waves

slides._comment: Wave 1 and Wave 2 as recommended actions
slides.title: Wave 1 and Wave 2 — foundation and core APM (Weeks 1–8)

columns.body: Export Datadog monitoring data and synthetic inventory before contract lapses. Compile facility host inventory. Define SLO targets with VP of IT and VP of Operations. Identify mission-critical endpoints. Name the technical DRI.
columns.subcopy: No Dynatrace deployment required — unblocks every downstream wave

columns.body: Deploy Synthetic monitors on all mission-critical endpoints. Configure SLOs and red/green availability dashboards. Enable Web RUM for visitor behavior baseline.
columns.subcopy: Low disruption — no host agents or code changes. Delivers the technical team's top priorities immediately

columns.body: Deploy OneAgent® on breadSHIP and breadSAIL. Non-production pilot for 5 days; then production with a documented rollback plan. Validate host coverage across all 30 facilities.
columns.subcopy: Gate: named technical DRI required before this wave begins

slides.title: Wave 3 and Wave 4 — mobile intelligence and Davis AI validation (TBD)

columns.body: Deploy Mobile RUM SDK into the mobile ordering app. Configure Business Events for the mobile conversion funnel and for breadSHIP/breadSAIL logistics outcomes.
columns.subcopy: Begins only after Wave 2 is stable in production. Timeline contingent on mobile engineering contact and app release cadence confirmation (IA-06)

columns.body: Allow Davis AI 30-day baselining period. Compare mean time to detect (MTTD) against the Datadog baseline from the pre-deployment export.
columns.subcopy: Requires sufficient OneAgent coverage to produce meaningful signal. Validates the MTTD improvement claim with a measured before/after

columns.body: Waves are serialized — Hannah's technical team is extremely change-averse. Running simultaneous instrumentation tracks across three systems is the scenario most likely to produce a stop-work call.
columns.subcopy: One wave stable before the next begins — non-negotiable

slides.eyebrow: Decision required — five asks before migration begins
slides.title: Five leadership decisions needed in the first five days
content: VP of IT — Day 1: Approve export of all Datadog monitoring data before the contract lapses. Without this data, the migration ROI baseline disappears permanently
VP of IT — Day 3: Name a technical DRI with production deployment authority for breadSHIP and breadSAIL. Without a named DRI, Wave 2 cannot begin — and Waves 3 and 4 are also blocked
VP of IT + VP of Operations — Day 5: Approve SLO targets for all three applications. Requires a target-setting workshop with application owners — not just a platform configuration task
CTO — Day 5: Approve full Dynatrace SaaS implementation scope and confirm a mobile engineering contact. Wave 3 timing is TBD until this is resolved
VP of Operations — Day 5: Provide the national expansion plan (facilities, timeline, geographies). Without this, national expansion readiness cannot be instrumented and remains an unmeasured KPI

slides.title: Key risks — three require immediate action
content: HIGH — Datadog contract lapses before data export: the MTTD improvement baseline is lost permanently. Mitigation: approve IA-01 on Day 1; escalate immediately if Datadog admin access is restricted

HIGH — No technical DRI named: Wave 2 is blocked indefinitely and a production deployment on mission-critical logistics systems with no accountable internal owner is not acceptable. Mitigation: DA-03 is a leadership ask at the kickoff meeting
MEDIUM — SLO targets set too tight trigger an immediate breach state, eroding trust in Dynatrace on Day 1. Mitigation: start all SLOs at 99.0%; schedule a formal review after 30 days of live data
MEDIUM — Mobile app release cadence incompatible with Wave 3 timeline. Mitigation: IA-06 by Day 5; if quarterly cadence is confirmed, communicate the timeline slip to leadership immediately
MEDIUM — Simultaneous Wave 2 and Wave 3 would overwhelm the change-averse team. Mitigation: waves are serialized — Wave 3 does not start until Wave 2 is stable in production

slides.title: Appendix — top hypotheses by ICE score
content: H3-B (ICE 18.67): Zero facility host monitoring — confirmed greenfield gap; high confidence, low effort to discover once OneAgent deployed
H6-C (ICE 15.75): No SLO tracking — availability SLO absence confirmed; highest confidence (greenfield), medium effort to configure once targets agreed
H5-B (ICE 14.40): No synthetic monitoring — zero Dynatrace synthetics confirmed; Datadog coverage scope pending; high impact on MTTD
H1-C (ICE 14.00): No cross-channel session stitching — web-to-mobile user journeys are invisible; low effort to configure once RUM is live
H2-A (ICE 9.00): breadSHIP latency bottleneck — high impact but confidence bounded by greenfield context; no Dynatrace trace data yet to validate
